title: BLM-CO TRFO BASIN WELL AND WATER SYSTEM
description: BLM-CO TRFO BASIN WELL AND WATER SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS This is a solicitation announcement for well improvements of a well house located at the Bureau of Land Management TRFO Basin Well, Montrose County, Colorado near Naturita, CO. Socio-economic Categories: While this procurement will be solicited only to the C-MAC Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises. 1.1 PROJECT DESCRIPTION Contractor shall provide a turnkey solar powered, well water system that automatically provides and maintains water to a wildlife drinking tank with minimal human input except winterization and annual maintenance. System shall be designed to have a solar pumping system at an existing water well. Provide water to an elevated buried storage tank. The buried storage tank will gravity feed the drinking tank. An additional tee and valve shall be provided for a future upgrade for a stockwater tank. System shall be designed to be freeze proof and operational in the winter to the frost free hydrant at the drinking tank. 1.2 LOCATION Latitude: 38.06529167� N Longitude: -108.63154723� W From Naturita, CO. Travel south on CO-141 for approximately 12 miles. Turn right (west) on County Road U29. Travel approximately 5 miles. The project is on the left (south). 1.3 WORK SCHEDULE Work shall be completed within 360 days of the Notice to Proceed. Contractor shall complete all work within 360 days of starting work. Work is not allowed on Federal holidays. Work shall occur Monday through Friday. Contract time will be paused, upon request, when snow or snowmelt prevents work at the project site. title: Chalk Rock Link Trail Project
description: This solicitation is restricted to Small Business. Project Description: The contractor will be required to clear and grub a trail corridor that is a minimum of 72-inches wide and 80-inches high within the designated path alignment. This work consists of clearing, grubbing, trimming, removing, and treating trees, logs, limbs, branches, brush, plants, and other vegetation within the clearing limits. Clearing practices must include removal down to ground level of any cedar tree that will be trimmed 25% or more. Furthermore, the contractor shall work to avoid any damage to existing, native Burr Oak trees. Cleared vegetation must be removed and piled near the staging area adjacent to the asphalt road for future USACE removal. The trail link will be approximately 2,250 linear feet of bench excavation and tread shaping to establish a stable tread base which follows the alignment in attached Drawing 1, which will be staked by USACE prior to mobilization. The finished trail tread width will range between 36 - 48-inches depending on location and terrain and will be topped with a 4-inch lift of mechanically compacted crushed gravel. The crushed gravel will be placed, graded, and mechanically compacted. Due to the terrain, the final path at minimum will consist of switchbacks with turning platforms to ensure a proper turn radii for both foot and bicycle traffic. The required grade average for the trail tread is 6-8% sustained with a max of 10-15% for no more than 30-foot intervals. Grade reversals and drainage features are required to be installed as preventative measures to promote long-term sustainability. At the halfway point of the trail link, a 4-foot by 8-foot gravel pad with a 4-inch mechanically compacted lift will be constructed adjacent to the trail path for future USACE placement of a cedar log bench. Ground disturbance outside of the clearing limits must be prevented. Significant ground disturbance outside of these limits will result in the contractor's need to perform remedial vegetation measures, as directed by USACE. Site Visit: A site visit is scheduled on August 24th at 10am local time. Contractors will meet at the Natural Resource and Outside Maintenance Facility and then travel to the work site. Please RSVP to communicate your intent to attend this meeting by emailing kelsey.m.kniffen@usace.army.mil by COB Friday, August 21. title: Fish Barrier Maintenance and Repair IDIQ
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number W912P626QA021 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Fish Barrier Repair and Maintenance Services. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically via PIEE. Refer to the attached solicitation in PIEE for the items, provisions, and clauses. The Contractor shall provide all labor, material, equipment, and supervision required to perform routine preventive maintenance, scheduled overhauls, diagnostic troubleshooting, and emergency repair services for the Electric Fish Dispersal Barrier System located on the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) in Romeoville, Will County, Illinois. Key technical requirements include: Preventive Maintenance: Monthly, quarterly, and annual inspections and servicing of high-voltage pulsers, power distribution panels, parasitic electrodes, backup generator systems, and system cooling arrays. Scheduled Repairs: Component replacement, structural repair of electrodes, and calibration of precision precision measuring, monitoring, and safety telemetry equipment. Emergency Repairs: Unscheduled rapid-response on-site troubleshooting within four (4) hours of notification to resolve system anomalies, power failures, or pulser dropouts that threaten barrier field integrity. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. All quotes must be submitted electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module at https://piee.eb.mil. No email, hand-delivered, or faxed proposals will be accepted.

title: FES Hovercraft
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) FES Hovercraft This announcement constitutes a Sources Sought Synopsis and Request for Information (RFI) to afford industry an opportunity to provide information regarding their capabilities to provide commercial items. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB), nor is it to be construed as a commitment by the U. S. Government to form a binding contract. Parties that respond will not be paid for the information submitted. The Air Force is hereby requesting capability statements and other information from interested sources. General Information: The 412 CS at the Air Force Test Center at Edwards AFB, CA is in the process of determining the acquisition strategy to obtain information from potential eligible and interested contractors for the purchase of FES Hovercraft. The AFTC anticipates awarding a contract under the associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) is 336612 with a standard employee size of 1000 and a Product Service Code (PSC) of 1940. A firm-fixed price contract will be contemplated. Salient Characteristics (Minimum Government Technical Requirements) Requirement Category -Minimum Acceptable Threshold (Government Minimum Need) Braking & Maneuverability -Must feature an active reverse-thrust braking system capable of redirecting at least 50�60% of engine thrust forward via fly-by-wire/cockpit controls. Payload Capacity -Minimum passenger capacity of six (6) personnel or an operational payload of not less than 1,000 lbs (453 kg) on cushion. Powerplant -Minimum 100 HP, multi-cylinder, liquid-cooled, fuel-injected engine with dual radiator cooling and electric start. Speed & Endurance -Minimum cruise speed of 35 mph; calm water speed greater than or equal to 45 mph; minimum operational range of 70+ miles on a standard fuel tank. Operating Temperature -Must function reliably across an ambient range of -30�F to +110�F (-34�C to +43�C). Buoyancy & Hull Safety -USCG-compliant positive flotation providing greater than or equal to 135% unladen displacement buoyancy with closed-cell composite urethane foam. Terrain Clearance -Minimum 8-inch hard structure obstacle clearance at operational hover power with segmented finger skirts. Emergency Integration -Factory-integrated emergency beacon/lightbar, siren/PA system, searchlight receptacle, and non-slip deck. Transportation & Deployment Requirements Dedicated Trailer: One (1) matching single-axle fly-on/fly-off tilt trailer equipped with hull-protection rollers and standard ball hitch. Rapid Deployment: The entire system must be capable of single-person launch and recovery from the trailer directly onto dry ground, mud, or water. Training & Technical Data Deliverables The contractor shall deliver: Operator Certification: On-site certified pilot training (Class 3 Pilot Certification curriculum) covering basic control, high-speed turning, reverse-thrust braking, and casualty extraction maneuvers. Maintenance Training: Factory or on-site maintenance instruction covering pre/post-flight inspections, skirt segment replacement, and engine servicing. Technical Manuals: Commercial operator, maintenance, and illustrated parts breakdown (IPB) manuals delivered at vehicle handover. System for Award Management (Sam.gov) registration is mandatory for this contract (see SAM website at (https://sam.gov/content/home). Responses will contribute to the Market Research Report as part of the acquisition strategy development process. Sources responding are invited to provide input and recommendations concerning contract type, contract clauses, and other aspects of the acquisition and anything else that may help to develop an efficient and effective acquisition strategy. If sufficient responsible and capable sources are identified, a formal RFQ will be posted on SAM.gov. Interested parties are requested to furnish a capability statement detailing their capabilities to provide these services, include highlights of experience on similar government or commercial contracts/agreements. In addition, please indicate business size (Large or Small), CAGE code/DUNS, provide a list of any contracts or other agreements similar in nature, the program/project name, contract number or other identifier, administering office/address, and the point of contact with the current telephone number. The AFTC will not pay for information or comments provided and will not recognize any cost associated with submission of comments. Please provide your response in Microsoft Word or a Microsoft Word compatible format. Submissions should be to the point and no more than 10 double space pages. Responses shall not be proprietary and will be unclassified. Interested vendors should submit responses no later than 09 Sep 2026 12:00 P.M. Pacific Daylight Time (PDT). Small Business sources responding should state their business size status based on the NAICS referenced above. Replies to this RFI should be sent via email to Melissa Alvarez, Contract Specialist, AFTC/PZIOA at melissa.alvarez.2@us.af.mil and cc: Steven Confer, Contracting Officer, AFTC/PZIOA at steven.confer@us.af.mil.

title: Commercial Internet Services for Unaccompanied Housing (UH) Dormitories
description: *Amendment to update SECTION V � EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD in attachment Combo RFQ_UH WiFi_v2* This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a commercial service prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12.202, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA461026Q0049 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for Provide and install Commercial Internet Services for Unaccompanied Housing (UH) Dormitories at Vandenberg Space Force Base (VSFB). The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide modems, routers, switches, software and services as described in the Statement of Work (SOW) at VSFB. Service should also include upgrading the hardware in the Titan (Bldg 13135) telecommunication room and disposal of old hardware. The Contractor shall use existing infrastructure to the greatest extent possible. The broadband internet access provided shall exceed 100Mbps download and 20Mbps upload. The Contractor should install a landing page required to access the internet. The landing page will clearly describe the terms and conditions, and force user login prior to internet access being granted. The contractor will also set up content filtering for inappropriate material as determined by the SLD 30 Commander. Any DOD portable electronic devices must comply with Section 3.4 of DOD Instruction 8420.01. New cables and hardware will need to be installed in common areas (dayrooms, laundry room, ectara). This acquisition is 100 percent set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The applicable NAICS code for this acquisition is 517111, and the applicable PSC is DG11, the size standard of 1,500 employees. The Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) rating program does not apply to this acquisition. This RFQ is NOT to be construed as a commitment by the United States Air Force. The Government is NOT liable for any costs and/or activity associated with providing a response to this announcement. Any costs incurred as a result of a response to this announcement shall be borne by the firm and will not be charged to the government for reimbursement. The Government reserves the right to award some or all of the line items represented herein. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse for costs associated with providing a quote. Any questions are due no later than 12:00 PM (PDT) Friday, 28 August 2026 Quotations are due no later than 12:00 PM (PDT) Wednesday, 9 September 2026 Any questions or offers shall be submitted via email to Contract Specialist, Jessica Rowe at jessica.rowe.5@spaceforce.mil , and Contracting Officer, Kristofer Clark at kristofer.clark@spaceforce.mil.

The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service providers performing the services herein. Such contract service providers shall be accountable solely to the Contractor who, in turn, is responsible to the Government. 1.2 Description of Services/Introduction: The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services (NPS) necessary to perform the repair, maintenance, rekeying/recombination, relocation, and technical support for safe & vault servicing as defined in this Statement of Work (SOW), except for those items specified as Government-furnished property and services. The Contractor shall perform to the standards in this SOW. 1.3 Background: The Southern Arizona VA Health Care System (SAVAHCS), Tucson VA Medical Center (VAMC) uses safes & vaults across multiple departments to secure sensitive items. These assets require preventive maintenance (PM) to function at peak performance levels, repair services when something malfunctions, and technical support for changing entry codes or re-keying. title: HSMR/SOAR Training
description: Special Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source Synopsis IAW RFO 12.201-1 The 767 Enterprise Sourcing Flight on Barksdale Air Force Base hereby submits an intent to award a sole source contract. The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-priced contract to A6A Associates utilizing Simplified Acquisition Procedures as authorized by FAR 12.201-1. This combined synopsis/solicitation has been tailored to comply with the requirements of RFO 5.101(a)(1) and FAR 12.201-1. Description/Purpose: The required service is a comprehensive, two-day medical readiness training program meticulously designed to equip Air Force Medical Treatment Facilities (MTFs) with the skills and knowledge necessary to achieve and maintain optimal readiness for all-hazards emergencies. The training's primary objective is to sustain and enhance both the Medical Contingency Response Plan (MCRP) and Home Station Medical Response Readiness (HSMR) capabilities within the MTFs. This training must be executed in full compliance with stringent regulatory and procedural guidelines, specifically: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Administrative Instruction 6055.02, DoDI 6200.03, AFI 10-2501, AFI 10-2519, AFI 41-106, and AFTTP 3-42.32. The program will provide Air Force leaders and staff with the knowledge of USAF and Air Force Medical Service (AFMS) procedures for effective medical response to installation incidents. A critical element of the training is enhancing performance assessment capabilities through the comprehensive implementation and reinforcement of the Response Training and Assessment Program (RTAP) tools. This empowers team chiefs to systematically evaluate the performance of their MCRP teams against established mission requirements and the defined Concept of Operations (CONOPS). The training will emphasize the practical application and thorough analysis of RTAP results, enabling the identification of specific areas requiring improvement and facilitating targeted corrective actions. The training program further provides robust support to Air Force MTFs in adapting to the evolving landscape of Emergency Management requirements, including HSMR, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (C-CBRN) defense, and Public Health Emergencies. The training encompasses a detailed assessment of MTF capabilities across the all-hazards spectrum. This is achieved through targeted training and realistic exercise scenarios in key areas, including (but not limited to): Mass Prophylaxis Point of Dispensing (POD) exercises Public Health Team Training (including Session II) Foodborne Illness Investigation Exercises Bioenvironmental Engineering Training White Powder Response Drills POD Walk Through Sessions Biological Agent Response Tabletop Exercises Medical Control Center (MCC) Operations Medical Command and Control (C2) and Patient Tracking Exercises Field Response Team Training Disaster Mental Health Team Training Triage Team Training Clinical Team Training Aircraft Mishap Full-Scale Exercises Active Shooter Awareness Training Evacuation and Shelter-In-Place Healthcare Setting procedures MTF Recall and Accountability Drills Mass Warning Notification Tabletop Exercises (including Mass Warning Notification System Protocols) Active Shooter Full Scale Exercises First Receivers Awareness Training First Receivers Operations Training C-CBRN Mass Casualty Full-Scale Exercises MTF Operations in a CBRN Environment Continuity of Operations (COOP) Planning Workshops and Tabletop Exercises Hospital Incident Command System (HICS) Training Patient Evacuation Full-Scale Exercises Lack of competition justification: A6A Associates is the proprietary owner and sole provider of the Sustainment Operations for AFMS Responders (SOAR) training platform within the commercial marketplace and does not have authorized resellers.The SOAR concept includes several proprietary and unique methodologies and tools designed by A6A, including: The CODE SILVER tabletop exercise methodology Scenario-specific process (chemical, aircraft mishap, public health emergency) analytical patient tracking and proprietary scientifically-developed casualty/patient simulation cards The SOAR HSMR Exercise Outcomes process (chemical, aircraft mishap, public health emergency). A6A is the only company with the qualifications to deliver a SOAR training. No other company possesses the concept, the materials, the experience and the proprietary methodologies. Market research was conducted and it has confirmed that the above company is able to meet the government's needs. Accordingly, a sole source award will be made to A6A Associates. Notice to potential offerors: This notice does not constitute a solicitation document. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency for future acquisitions. All information received after publication of this notice will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice. The Government will not pay for information received. Firms who desire to challenge this sole source action must submit an interest letter (email is acceptable) that demonstrates technical expertise, certifications, and authorization to compete for this acquisition. The letter must describe clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government and will not be cost or time prohibitive. Any questions regarding this synopsis should be directed to: Capt Grosshaeuser, Contracting Officer, at zachary.grosshaeuser@us.af.mil, (318)-456-8686

title: Stable Optical Cavity Absolute Reference System
description: This is a Notice of Proposed Contract Action under RFO Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. This notice is for information only; a solicitation will not be issued. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION. No contract will be awarded on the basis of offers received in response to this notice. The associated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 334516 (Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing) with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The Government requires the procurement of a Stable Optical Cavity Absolute Reference System, and intends to negotiate a sole-source award for this requirement with Stable Laser Systems, 4946 63rd Street Suite B, Boulder, CO, 80301-3285. Relevant part numbers and associated product descriptions are as follows: Item 1, qty. 1 each � Part #: 6010-4 Cylinder Cavity Assembly Item 2, qty. 1 each � Part #: VH6010-4 Vacuum Housing for Cylinder Cavity Assembly Item 3, qty. 1 each � Part #: N/A Measurement of Zero Crossing Temperature of Notched Cavity Assembly Item 4, qty. 1 each � Part #: N/A Temperature Controller Unit Item 5, qty. 1 each � Part #: N/A Ion Pump Unit The Government has determined that other companies' products do not meet or cannot be modified to meet the Government's needs. Stable Laser Systems is the only known commercial vendor capable of offering a Stable Optical Cavity Absolute Reference System that meets the Government's following essential requirements: Item 1 � Cylinder Cavity Assembly Spacer Specifications: 50 mm outer diameter x 100 mm length, FSR between 1.4-1.6 GHz, Premium grade ULE glass to stabilize a laser to drift less than 0.1 MHz/day Mirror Pair Specifications: ULE glass 1� diameter x 0.25� thick plano/plano, ULE glass 1� diameter x 0.25� thick concave/plano with 50 cm radius of curvature. Super polished finish on S1 and a surface quality of 10-5 or better, S2 will have a surface quality of 20-10 or better. Mirror coating specifications on side S1 of mirrors Operational wavelength: 493 nm and 650 nm simultaneously Finesse: between 750 - 2000 S2 AR percentage at normal incidence: less than 0.25% Item 2 � Vacuum Housing for Cylinder Cavity Assembly includes Zerodur mounting block with viton balls positioned (with recess). Vacuum can with notch for mounting block. Indium seal on the back flange and O-ring seal on the front flange. Thermal insulation and outer shell with heaters and thermistors. 1.33� Conflat tee is provided for coupling to vacuum components positioned on the back flange. Windows will be AR coated as in Line #1. The cavity is horizontal with equivalent optical access from either end of the vacuum housing. Vacuum housing pressure to be at least 10^-7 Torr or less Thermistor model to be used: MC65F103BTuning range: 1480 - 1640 nm or wider Item 3 � Measurement of Zero Crossing Temperature of Notched Cavity Assembly A frequency vs temperature graph will be provided for optimal cavity temperature use. Optimal cavity temperature must be above dew point and below 150 C. Item 4 � Temperature Controller Unit Temperature controller must be compatible with system and can tune vacuum housing to the zero-crossing temperature measured in Line #3. Item 5 � Ion Pump Unit Ion pump, controller, HV cable to connect ion pump to ion pump controller, Valve to connect to 1.33� Conflat tee. Must pump system down to 10^-7 Torr or less as described in line #2 Market research yielded that the majority of standard optical suppliers do not offer these types of highly specialized systems. One alternate vendor identified during market research offers optical reference cavities that meet the majority of the above-outlined specifications, but for the operational wavelength. The required operational wavelengths, as stated above, are 493 nm and 650 nm simultaneously, whereas the alternate vendor�s optical reference cavity operates at a wavelength above 1500 nm. Considering this, and also considering that Stable Laser Systems indicated that they are the sole manufacturer of the system and do not maintain an active network of resellers, a sole-source award to Stable Laser Systems is contemplated, as aforementioned. This is a notice of proposed contract action and not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement or proposal, which shall be considered by the agency. All inquiries should be sent by email to Tabitha.Haggart@us.af.mil. Responses must be submitted by the date/time listed on the notice. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government in future procurements. Responses received will be evaluated; however a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government anticipates an award on or before 30 September 2026. A Sole Source Justification will be attached to the subsequent Notice of Award in accordance with applicable regulation.

title: DA10--Pre-Solicitation Notice with Intent to Sole Source R&D VR Tech Support Services for Immersive VR Training Tool Modification and Maintenance
description: Pre-Solicitation Notice for the notice of intent to award a sole source contract. This is not a solicitation. The Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Research and Development (R&D), Regional Procurement Office (RPO) East in Pittsburgh, PA intends to award on a sole source basis a Firm-Fixed-Price Contract for a one (1) year base period to include two (2) option years to XRtistry LLC, 5536 Linn Road, Amherst, OH 44001 for R&D Custom VR Tech Support Services for Immersive VR Training Tool Modification and Maintenance. XRtistry is the only known vendor that can provide the R&D VR Tech Support Services for Immersive VR Training Tool Modification and Maintenance required by the Louis Stokes Cleveland VA Medical Center (LSCVAMC) in support of ongoing research projects as the original custom software application developer. The software is not available to purchase on the open market and contains proprietary intellectual property. The VA research team requires additional tech support services to modify and upgrade the original custom software for use in home settings by Veterans participating in a randomized clinical trial for impairment due to traumatic brain injury. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities. The applicable NAICS code is 541511 Custom Computer Programming Services with a $34.0 million size standard. The PSC is DA10. The authority for this action is RFO FAR 6.103-1 only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. title: W912P626QA021 Fish Barrier Maintenance and Repair IDIQ
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number W912P626QA021 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Fish Barrier Repair and Maintenance Services. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically via PIEE. Refer to the attached solicitation in PIEE for the items, provisions, and clauses. The Contractor shall provide all labor, material, equipment, and supervision required to perform routine preventive maintenance, scheduled overhauls, diagnostic troubleshooting, and emergency repair services for the Electric Fish Dispersal Barrier System located on the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) in Romeoville, Will County, Illinois. Key technical requirements include: Preventive Maintenance: Monthly, quarterly, and annual inspections and servicing of high-voltage pulsers, power distribution panels, parasitic electrodes, backup generator systems, and system cooling arrays. Scheduled Repairs: Component replacement, structural repair of electrodes, and calibration of precision precision measuring, monitoring, and safety telemetry equipment. Emergency Repairs: Unscheduled rapid-response on-site troubleshooting within four (4) hours of notification to resolve system anomalies, power failures, or pulser dropouts that threaten barrier field integrity. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. All quotes must be submitted electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module at https://piee.eb.mil. No email, hand-delivered, or faxed proposals will be accepted.

title: HAARP large scale blast testing and fragmentation characterization
description: Background The Department�s Bureau of Diplomatic Security, Physical Security Division, Research and Development Branch (DS/PSD/RD) is investigating debris generated from perimeter anti-ram barriers during a Vehicle Borne Improvised Explosive Device (VBIED) attack. DS/PSD/RD is seeking proposals to conduct large scale blast testing and fragmentation tracking. Government Furnished Information to Performer: DOS DS PSD Standard Practice for Blast Tests Final report and test data from previous anti-ram barrier debris characterization testing Physical Security Handbook (Red Book) drawing templates Scope This effort will be broken into two phases. Phase 1 will be to evaluate and characterize the debris generated from a simulated VBIED attack against baseline Department anti-ram systems, identified in this document. Phase 2 will be to evaluate and characterize debris generated from modified Department anti-ram systems. Performers will be evaluated on: Ability to perform testing in accordance with Blast Testing SOP for DS/PSP/PSD Responders shall provide a narrative for test site setup as part of performer evaluation. Test facility capabilities: Topography suitable for instrumentation Large, clear, flat, and level test spaces are ideal to best characterize the debris: Ability to characterize dynamic debris at 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Ability to character debris at rest post test (as far as 1,500ft from initial test article location) Free of debris from previous tests Widths that can accommodate HS camera views that capture overall events A 2,000 lbs. TNT NEW range limit is the minimum required to conduct this testing. DS/PSD/RD will accept either single test article test, or if appropriate, test two test articles simultaneously as seen in Figure 1: Will require larger test range, ~3,000ft Figure 1: Example of Setup to Test Two Anti-Ram Fences in One Test Instrumentation plan: Required to characterize debris generated from the anti-ram barriers: At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, 300ft, and at rest Characterize the following from debris: Dimensions Weight Velocity Height from ground Dispersion Plan to differentiate debris from one test to the next (concrete dye, paint, etc.) and/or clear range of debris from prior tests DS/PSD/RD has no prescribed methodology to capture the above data; The performer shall propose their instrumentation and post processing plans including the types of data acquisition equipment and any software needed to do the analysis. Schedule: Complete the project within 24 months, with more consideration given to condensed schedules. Compressed testing dates are preferred to avoid excess testing travel lengths or multiple trips. DS/PSD/RD Understands cost and schedule need to be balanced. Testing two anti-ram fences simultaneously saves time, explosives, and setup labor but requires duplicate instrumentation and a much larger test range. Performer should provide their plan and justify. Performer is also welcome to provide several; approaches and let DS/PSD/RD decide which is most advantageous to the government. Phase 1: Initial Anti-Ram Barrier Debris Characterization: Set up: For planning purposes, the surrogate Vehicle Borne Improvised Explosive Device will be a charge with the NEW of 2,000lbs TNT, in a cylinder with a L/D of 1, sat atop a 32in table, centered on a 10ft x 10ft concrete pad, and placed so that there is a 24in gap between the edge of charge and the test article. The boundary conditions of the test articles will influence the amount of debris generated during the testing, but the government needs to balance cost with real world simulation. Therefore, the government would like the performer to provide options to build and test the test articles in lengths of 30ft, 45ft and 60ft long sections and constructed per the drawings in Appendix A. Figure 2: Example Test Article Layout Phase 1 Test Articles: Test Sample Design Being Tested Drawings in Appendix B Brief Description (See Appendix A for Details) Potential to Combine tests Length of Test sample Options Base 1 AC-41-05 Bar Fence on top of DS-50 Knee Wall 20x20mm Bars @ 65mm OC N B1.1: 30ft B1.2: 45ft B1.3:60ft Base 2 AC-41-06 Picket Fence on top of DS-50 Knee Wall 50mm x 6mm Pickets @200mm OC N B2.1: 30ft B2.2: 45ft B2.3:60ft Base 3 DS-40 Anti- Climb & Ram Fence 20x20mm Bars @ 130 mm OC w/ DN250 XS Pipes @ 1,720mm OC Yes w/ base 4 or Option 2 B3.1: 30ft B3.2: 45ft B3.3:60ft Base 4 DS-44 Steel Anti- Climb & Ram Fence 100mm x 50mm x 6mm Tubes @ 175mm OC Yes w/ base 3 or Option 2 B4.1: 30ft B4.2: 45ft B4.3:60ft Option 1 AC-41-04 Tube Fence on top of DS-50 Knee Wall 38mm dia. x 3mm Tubes @150mm OC N O1.1: 30ft O1.2: 45ft O1.3:60ft Option 2 DS-43 Steel Anti- Climb & Ram Fence with Kickers 100mm x 50mm x 6mm Tubes @ 175mm OC with Kickers @ 350mm OC Yes w/ base 2 or base 3 O2.1: 30ft O2.2: 45ft O2.3:60ft After the Phase 1 test data will be analyzed by the performer and DS/PSD will determine which test samples produced the most and least hazardous fragmentation based of level of hazardous debris produced. Phase 2: Modified Anti-Ram Barrier Debris Characterization: In certain scenarios the Department requires perimeters to employ opaque barriers to prevent easy external observation. To meet this requirement the test samples that produced the least hazardous fragmentation in Phase 1 will be fitted with various opaque claddings and tested to determine which produce the least hazardous fragmentation. The performer will research various opaque claddings that will provide concealment with preference to those that would mitigate and reduce the level of hazardous debris generated. The performer will research and propose feasible fence and knee-wall cladding materials that can be tested in Phase 2. The criteria for potential fence cladding are: Opaque Weather resistant Aesthetically pleasing Potential to break up in a non-hazardous way Large yet low mass pieces Small pieces Consumed by VBIED�s thermal energy Etc. Readily available construction materials Cost effective and easily constructable Test Sample Design Being Tested Example Cladding Options will be Researched and Suggested by Performer and Accepted by DS/PSD/RD Potential to Combine tests Length of Test sample Options Option 3 Best Performing Fence on knee wall with opaque cladding E.g.: 24-gauge stainless steel 316L or Alum equivalent decorative panel on fence and steel plate behind knee wall N O3.1: 30ft O3.2: 45ft O3.3:60ft Option 4 Best Performing Fence on knee wall with opaque cladding E.g.: Metal plate material on fence and knee wall N O4.1: 30ft O4.2: 45ft O4.3:60ft Option 5 Best Performing Anti-Ram Fence with Opaque cladding E.g.: Stainless steel 316L or Alum equivalent decorative panel on fence Yes w/ Option 6 O5.1: 30ft O5.2: 45ft O5.3:60ft Option 6 Best Performing Anti-Ram Fence with Opaque cladding E.g.: Light weight material Yes w/ Option 5 O6.1: 30ft O6.2: 45ft O6.3:60ft Deliverables Test Data: The performer will determine the best method to place video cameras, gauges, surveying equipment, etc. necessary to capture the desired data. The performer shall present their instrumentation plan to DS for feedback and approval prior to the test. Dynamic data to be collected is as follows: HS Video: Overall Event and downrange point of view (e.g. at 1,000ft) At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft and 300ft Dimension/description of debris (steel, concrete, steel and concrete, etc.) At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Estimated weight of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Velocity of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft and 300ft Height of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Dispersion pattern of debris At 75ft, 100ft, 200ft, and 300ft Post blast debris assessment will be conducted to characterize the debris. The performer shall determine the search area necessary to capture 90% of the debris weighing one pound or more (estimated to be 1,000ft to 1,500ft from originating position but performer needs to confirm). Data to be collected: Dimensions of debris/

title: CO NP ROMO 407(1) Holzwarth Culvert
description: THIS IS NOT AN INVITATION FOR BID, PLAN AND SPECIFICATIONS ARE NOT AVAILABLE PROJECT NUMBER: CO NP ROMO 407(1) PROJECT NAME: Holzwarth Culvert PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This project will replace the deficient Holzwarth Culvert (Structure No. 1520-029S), a six-barrel corrugated metal arch pipe culvert on the Holzwarth Access Road with a steel girder bridge. Located in Rocky Mountain National Park, approximately nine miles north of Grand Lake, CO, along US HWY 34 at an elevation of 8,900 feet, the culvert conveys flow from the Colorado River and provides access to the Holzwarth Historic Site. The purpose of this project is to prevent future roadway damage and flooding while maintaining access to employee housing, the historic site, and National Park Service and Forest Service recreation opportunities. SCOPE OF THE WORK: The project will consist of removal of the existing six barrel culvert and construction of a new steel girder bridge with a cast in place concrete deck. New bridge abutments and micropiles. Temporary stream diversion and riprap. New aggregate roadway surfacing. Relocation of an existing electrical line. Relocation of existing historic head gates into a new concrete slab. Access to the site is through a gate at the south end of the Holzwarth Historic Site Parking Lot and along the Holzwarth Culvert Access Road. The Holzwarth Culvert Access Road is approximately 13� wide with tight turns. Temporary widening will be necessary to prevent truck off tracking on to sensitive environmental resources. A temporary truck turnaround will also be necessary as no construction access is allowed more than 100� west of the bridge. PRINCIPAL WORK ITEMS: 20304-2000 Removal of Bridge: 1 EACH 30202-2000 Roadway Aggregate, Method 2: 120 TON 55504-0000 Prefabricated Steel Bridge (10� wide x 48� long modular steel vehicular bridge): 1 LPSM 56701-0000 Micropile (8.68� dia.): 180 LNFT 62801-0000 Temporary Stream Diversion: 1 LPSM ANTICIPATED SCHEDULE: Advertisement � September 2026 Award � December 2026 NTP � December 2026 Contract Completion � November 2027 ESTIMATED COST RANGE: Total estimated cost between $700,000 and $2,000,000.

description: Purpose: The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gauge industry interest and capability in performing portions of the Performance Work Statement (PWS) on a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) basis to support the Atlantic Undersea Test and Evaluation Center (AUTEC) contract. The PWS is grouped by three separate operation groups: Base Operations, Enterprise Operations, and Test Operations. The current contract number is N6660422C0102, and the prime contractor is Amentum Services Inc. AUTEC is the U.S. Navy�s Large-Area, Deep-Water, Undersea T&E Range within DoD�s Major Range and Test Facility Base (MRTFB). The range is located at Andros Island, Commonwealth of the Bahamas (AUTEC/Andros). The contract requires the contractor to supply a highly capable technical workforce who will operate and maintain unique tracking and instrumentation systems to support Navy Developmental and Fleet Training and Readiness Missions. Additionally, the contract establishes the contractor responsible for operation of a self-sufficient one square mile Navy outpost. The tasking is summarized at a high-level as follows: Base Operations on the AUTEC contract includes public works, logistic support, the maintenance/repair/construction of real property and grounds for AUTEC/Andros sites, Permanent-Party Housing, food services, emergency and firefighting services, and solid waste and recycling, in addition to other operation services (please review the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS) for further details). Enterprise Operations encompasses all functions related to General Information Management and Services sustaining AUTEC in the performance of its mission. Enterprise Operations includes the following: program management, oversight and accountability, business operations, management and operation of an effective electronic data interchange system, program documentation support, security, personnel security, industrial/information security, physical/operation/cyber security, Communication security, safety/environmental/energy and water management program support, air-passenger support, in addition to other operation services ( please review the attached PWS for further details). Test Operations are conducted based upon requirements set in Government provided test plans. Test operations include the following: planning/resource scheduling, range systems operations, post mission processing and analysis, and independent test operations systems (marine systems, helicopter services, Acoustic Tracking Equipment (ATE), Underwater Targets, etc.), in addition to other operation services (please review the attached PWS for further details) List of Attachments for this RFI Attachment 1: N6660422C0102 Performance Work Statement (PWS) Attachment 2: N6660422C0102 Workload Factor *Note that the attached PWS and Workload Factor represents the current contract. While updates are underway for new requirements, no major changes are anticipated. NOTE: The RFI attachments are Distribution D, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). See below and all attachments for full information and details regarding this RFI. You must request access to the attachment by clicking on its title and providing the reason you need access. You will not receive immediate access to view the document. Required CMMC level is Level 2 (Self). Active registration with the System for Award Management (SAM) is required, pursuant to applicable regulations and guidelines. A controlled attachment requires special handling due to the information it contains. The requestor must have a data entry or administrator role within the Contract Opportunities domain for an entity in SAM.gov in order to request access. If you do not have a proper role, you can request it from an existing entity administrator or have the existing administrator assign roles directly to you. Respondents are requested to address the following questions regarding the potential FFP Operation Services in their response to the Government. If so, provide details as to the nature and degree of the reservations and to which tasks or subtask or lower levels they apply. title: VHX-X1 Digital Microscope Solicitation
description: The Commander Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC) Procurement Group, Patuxent River, MD 20670 hereby gives notice of their intent to award a purchase order to Keyence Corporation of America, 669 DR Suite 403, Elmwood Park, New Jersey 07407-1361 (Cage: 0VZL5) on a sole source basis in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.102(a), only one source reasonably available and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Metals and Ceramics Department of the Materials Engineering Division (MED) at Fleet Readiness Center Southeast (FRCSE) requires the procurement of a specific type of fully integrated, turnkey digital microscope (VHX-X1) system to meet critical inspection and analysis needs. Current analysis methods are limited, and a system with unique capabilities, such as real-time 3D composition, advanced shadow-effect imaging for surface feature enhancement, and fully automated teaching functions, is required to analyze advanced materials and component failures. This procurement is for a new system that consolidates these proprietary functions into a single, integrated unit, replacing an older, less capable Keyence model. A trade-in of the existing equipment is included in this procurement. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which, if received within seven (7) calendar days after the date of the publication of this synopsis, will be considered. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The point of contact for this requirement is Ben Barton at benjamin.s.barton2.civ@us.navy.mil.

title: Nitrogen Generator Instrument Service Agreement
description: The purpose of this request is to acquire a new service agreement for the Nitrogen Generator (Model: Infinity XE6030, S/N: 722080281). Nitrogen generator provides a constant flow of high purity nitrogen gas to five Liquid Chromatograph/Mass Spectrometer (LC/MS) systems in the Division of Color Certification and Color Technology (DCCT). The LC/MS instruments are used to analyze batches of color additives intended for use in foods, drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics in the United States. DCCT uses the LC/MS instruments for trace level analysis (sub ppm levels) in color additives submitted for certification. Acquisition of a new service agreement for the Nitrogen Generator Instrument is urgent because the current warranty coverage has expired. Reliable and timely services, preventive maintenance, and repair services are critical for the instrument performance of the Nitrogen Generator. The Nitrogen Generator (Model: Infinity XE6030, S/N: 722080281) is essential to ensuring program continuity within the Color Certification Program, as it is used to determine whether each batch of color additive meets specifications outlined in 21 CFR Parts 74 and 82.

title: Domestic Datalink Services (DDLS) Market Survey 2
description: Domestic Datalink Services (DDLS) FY2026 Market Survey Synopsis The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is conducting a market survey to explore the development of Controller to Pilot Data Link Communication (CPDLC) services for airports and en route airspace following the expiration of the current Data Communication Integrated Services (DCIS) contract on September 30, 2029. This market survey is not a solicitation or a request for proposal but aims to gather information from industry stakeholders to inform future acquisition strategies. Background: CPDLC services are currently operational across all 20 Continental United States (CONUS) Centers, with Departure Clearance (DCL) services at 65 airports. These services are facilitated by the En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) system, which uses the Very High Frequency (VHF) Data Link Mode 2 (VDL-2) protocol for communication between air traffic controllers and FANS-equipped aircraft. The current DCIS contract is nearing its 14th year, and the FAA is considering establishing one or multiple 10-year contracts for future services. Program Objectives: The FAA seeks to ensure excellent, reliable end-to-end performance of CPDLC, gain timely insights into message statuses, obtain affordable services, introduce new technologies seamlessly, and facilitate a risk-minimized transition from DCIS to DDLS. Scope: The survey focuses on operational network services and associated monitoring, referred to as Data Communications Network Service (DCNS) under the current contract. Industry Participation: The FAA invites responses from interested parties with capabilities or interest in providing CPDLC services. Respondents are encouraged to share insights on acquisition design, operations, technical topics, and transition strategies from DCIS to DDLS. Key areas of interest include incentivizing performance, introducing new technologies, ensuring accurate monitoring, addressing technical and operational challenges, and facilitating seamless transitions. Response Guidelines: Interested parties must submit written responses in English, formatted as searchable PDFs, with "DDLS FY2026 Market Survey Response [Company Name]" in the subject line. Proprietary or confidential information should be clearly marked, and submissions should include contact details. Responses are due by September 9, 2026, and questions about the survey should be submitted by August 18, 2026. Future Activities: The FAA plans to conduct an Industry Day in late summer or early fall, providing opportunities for one-on-one sessions with interested parties. A Screening Information Request (SIR) for DDLS requirements is anticipated for release in the second quarter of FY2029. This market survey represents an opportunity for industry stakeholders to contribute to the shaping of future CPDLC services and to engage with the FAA in preparation for upcoming acquisition processes.

title: MQ9B SeaGuardian/SkyGuardian COCO Flight Services

Demonstrated experience providing COCO UAS or comparable aircraft flight services to the U.S. Government or other customers. Number and configuration of MQ-9B aircraft currently owned, leased, controlled, or otherwise available to support the requirement, including anticipated availability. Experience operating Group V UAS, including BVLOS operations, maritime operations, and operations in controlled/restricted airspace. Ability to provide qualified remote pilots, aircrew, maintenance personnel, GCSs, logistics, and other required support. Ability to operate from various OCONUS locations and one CONUS location. Standards required by NFPA 10 may include: Monthly Inspections: Check visibility and accessibility: Identify if a fire extinguisher is easily visible. It should not be blocked by any equipment or other objects that would make it difficult to be accessed during an emergency. If portable fire extinguishers other than wheeled types are inside an unlocked glass cabinet or similar containment unit, make sure that the access door is in serviceable condition. If not record on monthly record and include as part of documentation to the COR. Examine the physical state. Pick up the fire extinguisher to closely check for labeling, overall condition, and physical defects: Look for the fire extinguisher s serial number, and check if the fire extinguisher label is readable. Check if the cylinder and other external metal parts are free of corrosion, dents, and other signs of damage. Check the connection between the hose and cylinder is secure. 2.4.1.2.1.4. Check if the locking pin goes through the holes of the discharge lever and handle and if the pin is secured well by the seal. If there are items requiring replacement, replace the extinguishers and include as part of documentation to the COR. Inspection Tags or Labels. Each fire extinguisher shall have a tag or label securely attached that indicates that maintenance was performed. The tag, label, and/or verification-of-service collar located around the neck of the container will conform to NFPA guidelines. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source- Nitrogen Generator Instrument Service Agreement
description: The purpose of this request is to acquire a new service agreement for the Nitrogen Generator (Model: Infinity XE6030, S/N: 722080281). Nitrogen generator provides a constant flow of high purity nitrogen gas to five Liquid Chromatograph/Mass Spectrometer (LC/MS) systems in the Division of Color Certification and Color Technology (DCCT). The LC/MS instruments are used to analyze batches of color additives intended for use in foods, drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics in the United States. DCCT uses the LC/MS instruments for trace level analysis (sub ppm levels) in color additives submitted for certification. Acquisition of a new service agreement for the Nitrogen Generator Instrument is urgent because the current warranty coverage has expired. Reliable and timely services, preventive maintenance, and repair services are critical for the instrument performance of the Nitrogen Generator. The Nitrogen Generator (Model: Infinity XE6030, S/N: 722080281) is essential to ensuring program continuity within the Color Certification Program, as it is used to determine whether each batch of color additive meets specifications outlined in 21 CFR Parts 74 and 82.

title: Domestic Datalink Services (DDLS) Market Survey 2
description: Domestic Datalink Services (DDLS) FY2026 Market Survey Synopsis The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is conducting a market survey to explore the development of Controller to Pilot Data Link Communication (CPDLC) services for airports and en route airspace following the expiration of the current Data Communication Integrated Services (DCIS) contract on September 30, 2029. This market survey is not a solicitation or a request for proposal but aims to gather information from industry stakeholders to inform future acquisition strategies. Background: CPDLC services are currently operational across all 20 Continental United States (CONUS) Centers, with Departure Clearance (DCL) services at 65 airports. These services are facilitated by the En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) system, which uses the Very High Frequency (VHF) Data Link Mode 2 (VDL-2) protocol for communication between air traffic controllers and FANS-equipped aircraft. The current DCIS contract is nearing its 14th year, and the FAA is considering establishing one or multiple 10-year contracts for future services. Program Objectives: The FAA seeks to ensure excellent, reliable end-to-end performance of CPDLC, gain timely insights into message statuses, obtain affordable services, introduce new technologies seamlessly, and facilitate a risk-minimized transition from DCIS to DDLS. Scope: The survey focuses on operational network services and associated monitoring, referred to as Data Communications Network Service (DCNS) under the current contract. Industry Participation: The FAA invites responses from interested parties with capabilities or interest in providing CPDLC services. Respondents are encouraged to share insights on acquisition design, operations, technical topics, and transition strategies from DCIS to DDLS. Key areas of interest include incentivizing performance, introducing new technologies, ensuring accurate monitoring, addressing technical and operational challenges, and facilitating seamless transitions. Response Guidelines: Interested parties must submit written responses in English, formatted as searchable PDFs, with "DDLS FY2026 Market Survey Response [Company Name]" in the subject line. Proprietary or confidential information should be clearly marked, and submissions should include contact details. Responses are due by August 24, 2026, and questions about the survey should be submitted by August 3, 2026. Future Activities: The FAA plans to conduct an Industry Day in late summer or early fall, providing opportunities for one-on-one sessions with interested parties. A Screening Information Request (SIR) for DDLS requirements is anticipated for release in the second quarter of FY2029. This market survey represents an opportunity for industry stakeholders to contribute to the shaping of future CPDLC services and to engage with the FAA in preparation for upcoming acquisition processes.

The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) is seeking sources capable of providing Contractor Owned, Contractor Operated (COCO) MQ-9B SeaGuardian unmanned aircraft flight services in support of U.S. Navy and Department of War (DoW) missions. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The anticipated Period of Performance is five (5) years with an anticipated start date of September 2028. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT TYPE: Firm fixed price REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The Government anticipates that services may include maritime surveillance, anti-submarine warfare, and other Government-directed missions. The final requirement, performance locations, aircraft configuration, flight-hour requirements, period of performance, and contract structure will be established at the time of award, if this effort is pursued. The anticipated requirement is for contractor-provided MQ-9B SeaGuardian flight services, including, but not limited to: Provision of contractor-owned MQ-9B aircraft and associated Ground Control Station (GCS) capability; Qualified and appropriately certified pilots, mission operators, and maintenance personnel; Aircraft operation, launch and recovery, mission execution, and flight-hour support; Aircraft maintenance, logistics, spares, and supply support necessary to maintain mission availability; Mission planning, scheduling, and operational coordination; Communications, data links, and other equipment necessary to conduct assigned missions; Compliance with applicable Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DoW, U.S. Navy, airworthiness, range, and host-nation requirements, as applicable; Support for operations from designated CONUS and/or overseas locations and operating areas; and Other services necessary to provide a fully operational MQ-9B COCO flight-services capability. Demonstrated experience providing COCO UAS or comparable aircraft flight services to the U.S. Government or other customers. Number and configuration of MQ-9B aircraft currently owned, leased, controlled, or otherwise available to support the requirement, including anticipated availability. Experience operating Group V UAS, including BVLOS operations, maritime operations, and operations in controlled/restricted airspace. Ability to provide qualified remote pilots, aircrew, maintenance personnel, GCSs, logistics, and other required support. Ability to operate from various OCONUS locations and one CONUS location. Relevant contracts and programs demonstrating substantially similar capability. Known barriers, dependencies, or lead times associated with providing the requirements listed above Identification of any subcontracting or teaming arrangements interested companies believe could provide the required capability. All questions must be submitted via email to Chelsey Williams, chelsey.d.williams5.civ@us.navy.mil. title: Laser Measuring Machine Head Solicitation
description: The Commander Fleet Readiness Centers (COMFRC) Procurement Group, Patuxent River, MD 20670 hereby gives notice of their intent to award a purchase order to Pratt and Whittney Measurement Systems Inc., 66 Douglas St, Bloomfield, Connecticut 06002 USA (Cage: 3EQQ7) on a sole source basis in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.102(a), only one source reasonably available and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Fleet Readiness Center Southeast, located at Naval Air Station Jacksonville, Florida, utilizes a Laser Measuring Machine (LMM), Model TG2028-0025, to perform precision dimensional measurements in support of aircraft component manufacturing, inspection, and calibration operations. The LMM is critical to mission support and directly impacts accuracy and reliability. Maintaining optimal conditions supports workload continuity within the calibration laboratory and avoids disruptions to scheduled operations.The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, tools, equipment, transportation and any other items necessary to furnish and install one (1) LMM Laser Head. The installation, calibration, and testing must take place at FRCSE on NAS Jacksonville. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which, if received within seven (7) calendar days after the date of the publication of this synopsis, will be considered. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses received as a result of this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The point of contact for this requirement is Ben Barton at benjamin.s.barton2.civ@us.navy.mil.

The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. Offers are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 68HERW26Q0087 is issued as a �request for quotation (RFQ)� for a Liquid Chromatograph Triple Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer (LC/QQQ) with extended service plan options. Simplified procedures are being used and the anticipated award date is 9/27/2026. This acquisition is not set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 334516 - Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing, with a small business size standard in numbers of employees of 1,000. The product or service code is 6640 - Laboratory Equipment and Supplies. Extending Combined Synopsis to 09/09/26 @ 16:30 PM The VA at VAMC CWM (Central Western Massachusetts [Northampton/Leeds]) has requested the brand specific requirement for the Sorna Vertex 25ei Platform/CD Burner, Installation & Training Support, UPS 1KVA Tower, and published Training Manuals. The VA also noted that Delivery costs must be less than $250.00 or rolled into line-item pricing. VAMC CWM has standardized to the Sorna Vertex 25ei Platform and integrated CD Burner. The VA is requesting the Sorna brand Vertex 25ei Platform/CD Burner package; VAMC CWM has standardized to the Sorna Vertex 25ei Platform/CD Burner and the interconnecting PACS, VNA, RIS, and EMR systems. Standardization supports a request for brand name where an assurance for system integrity and system compatibility: fit, form, and function, are required to ensure full system functionality and integrity with existing PACS (Picture Archiving Communication System), VNA (Vendor Neutral Archive), RIS (Radiology Information System), and EMR (Electronic Medical Record) systems. Replacement with a name brand to which the service has standardized requires no additional accommodation or adaptations to ensure system integrity, system compatibility, and system functionality. Brand name replacement assures that the replacement product fully and directly integrates with the backup Sorna Vertex 25ei/CD Burner, and the existing PACS, VNA, RIS, and EMR systems. Replacement with a brand name, exact replacement, diminishes risk to patient care and treatment outcomes, and it preserves operational and cost efficiencies derived from standardization. A vendor is requesting consideration of a brand equal platform and CD Burner per FAR 11.105. FAR 11.105 states: An agency must not write requirements specifying a particular brand name, product, or feature unique to one manufacturer unless all three conditions are met: (a)(1) Essential to Government requirements Market research must clearly show that: Only that brand or feature meets the Government s minimum needs; and Other manufacturers similar items do not meet (and cannot be modified to meet) the requirement. (a)(2) Supported by a valid justification: FAR 12.102-1(a) justification (if using SAP [RFO]). title: Snow and Ice Removal
description: Request for Information (RFI) Snow and Ice Removal Services Market Research Notice The Bureau of Engraving and Printing (BEP) is conducting market research to identify qualified small business concerns interested in providing snow and ice removal services at the BEP Washington, DC Facility. The Government is also seeking industry feedback regarding the most appropriate fixed-price contract structure, pricing methodology, and acquisition vehicle for this requirement. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This is not a solicitation, request for proposal (RFP), or request for quotation (RFQ). Responses will be used to assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy and developing a future solicitation, if any. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in responding to this RFI. The attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the anticipated requirement for recurring snow and ice removal services at the Bureau of Engraving and Printing's Washington, DC Facility. The services include snow removal, ice treatment, snow hauling when required, and response to snow and ice events at approximately 102,700 square feet of sidewalks, driveways, parking areas, entrances, emergency exits, and other designated areas. Requested Information Interested small business concerns are requested to provide the following: Company Name. UEI. Business Size and Socioeconomic Status (if applicable). Confirmation that your company is interested in and capable of performing the attached draft PWS. A non-binding Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimate. Based on the attached draft PWS, identify the fixed-price contract structure your company believes would result in the greatest competition and the most reasonable pricing (e.g., per snow event, snowfall accumulation tiers, seasonal firm-fixed-price, or another fixed-price approach). Briefly explain your recommendation. Identify any provisions of the draft PWS or contemplated pricing methodology that may discourage competition or result in higher pricing. Confirm whether your company anticipates being able to comply with FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, if this requirement is set aside for small business. If your company holds a GSA contract, please identify the applicable contract vehicle(s) under which you could perform this requirement (e.g., Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), Building Maintenance and Operations (BMO), or both). Point of Contact (Name, Email Address, and Telephone Number). Responses should be limited to three (3) pages, excluding any cover page. Response Due Date Responses shall be submitted electronically to jerkendra.holloway@bep.gov no later than September 9, 2026 at 5:00 PM EST. Disclaimer This RFI is issued solely for planning and market research purposes. Responses are voluntary and will not be considered offers. The Government is under no obligation to issue a solicitation or award a contract based on this notice. Information received may be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy, contract structure, and procurement vehicle for any future solicitation.

title: J--Physical Access Control System (PACS) upgrade
description: This is a REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ)/Invitation for Bid (IFB)/Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought notice. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or IFB or RFP, if any is issued. The Government is seeking capable commercial systems integrators and security contractors to provide a turnkey Physical Access Control System (PACS) upgrade across federal law enforcement and administrative facilities during fiscal year 2027. The requirement is anticipated to be structured as a two-phase contract: Phase 1 (Assessment & Design): Perform site surveys, audit existing door hardware/power/network infrastructure, conduct a FICAM/ISC risk review, and deliver a 100% System Design Package. Phase 2 (Procurement, Installation, & Testing): Upon Government approval of the Phase 1 design, procure hardware, install FICAM-approved readers/controllers, run cabling, integrate head-end software/servers, perform testing, and train administrative personnel. Performance will occur across facilities situated in three primary geographic regions: Washington, DC Region: 1901 Anacostia Drive SE, Washington, DC 20020 (and associated district facilities) New York / Staten Island Region: 210 New York Ave, Staten Island, NY 10305 San Francisco, CA Region: 1217 Ralston Ave, San Francisco, CA 94129 In response to this sources sought, please provide the following by email to michelle_shoshone@ios.doi.gov 1. Company Name, Address, and Website: *Point of Contact: (Name, Title, Email, Phone Number) *Unique Entity ID (UEI) and CAGE Code: 2. Does your company have experience performing PACS assessments and designs compliant with Federal Identity, Credential, and Access Management (FICAM), HSPD-12, FIPS 201, and Interagency Security Committee (ISC) standards for federal law enforcement or detention/holding facilities? 3. Does your staff include engineers or designers holding CSEIP (Certified System Engineer ICAM Fellow), CPP, or PSP credentials? Please detail relevant certifications. 4. What open-architecture PACS platforms, head-end software, and GSA Approved Products List (APL) hardware (e.g., controllers, OSDP card readers) does your company typically install and integrate? 5. Can your company support a two-phase contract structure where Phase 1 is a Firm-Fixed-Price site assessment/design deliverable, and Phase 2 is executed via established unit pricing (per door/controller/reader/cable run) established at contract award? 6. Please describe your capability to perform on-site physical surveys and deployment across all three geographically dispersed regions (DC, NY, CA). Does your company maintain regional offices or certified technician networks near these locations? 7. How does your company handle high-security door hardware integration (e.g., heavy-duty electric strikes, magnetic locks, pneumatic sally port gates, request-to-exit devices, and intercom/duress systems) in law enforcement or holding environments? 8. What is your standard timeline for completing Phase 1 (site surveys and 100% design submittal) for three distinct multi-building locations upon receipt of Notice to Proceed (NTP)? 9. What is your typical turnaround time / installation lead time per facility once Phase 2 (procurement and physical work) is authorized and hardware is delivered? 10. Are your PACS hardware, design, and installation labor services available directly on your GSA MAS contract (e.g., under SINs 336320, 33411, or ANCILLARY), or via a GSA Contractor Team Arrangement (CTA)? 11. What standard commercial warranty is provided on both system hardware components and installation labor/craftsmanship? 12. What is your business size and socioeconomic status under NAICS 561621 (Security Systems Services $25.0M), NAICS 334111 (Computer Terminal/IT Hardware Manufacturing 1,250 employees), and/or NAICS 336320 (1,000 employees)? If you are a Large Business prime contractor, do you anticipate utilizing certified Small Business subcontractors for local cabling, installation labor, or ongoing maintenance in DC, NY, and CA?

description: 1. MINIMUM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS / SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS To be considered technically acceptable, the quoted product must meet or exceed all of the following minimum requirements: 1. Height: 60 inches 4. Electrical compatibility: must operate on standard facility power and must be compatible with 120V or 220V, maximum 60 amps. 5. Boiling chamber must be constructed of 316 stainless steel. 6. Equipment must be new. 7. Equipment must meet applicable federal and state environmental standards for vapor emissions and wastewater processing safety. 8. Minimum 1-year commercial warranty covering defects in materials and workmanship. 9. Contractor shall provide two (2) physical copies and one (1) digital copy of the operation and maintenance manual with each delivered unit. 5. DELIVERY Delivery shall be FOB Destination. All six (6) units shall be delivered in full within 100 days after receipt of order (ARO). Delivery Address: U.S. Coast Guard Sector Northern New England 259 High Street South Portland, ME 04106 All six (6) units shall be delivered to South Portland, Maine. The contractor must ensure the delivery vehicle configuration allows safe offload with a standard-size forklift. Delivery date and time shall be coordinated at least seven (7) business days in advance. 6. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE Inspection and acceptance will be performed by the Government at destination by the designated Quality Assurance Inspector (QAI) and/or other authorized Government personnel. Acceptance will be based on: a. Absence of visible shipping or transit damage; b. Confirmation that the delivered units meet the required technical characteristics; and c. Receipt of required manuals and warranty documentation. 7. QUOTE SUBMISSION Quotes shall be submitted electronically by email to Jeffrey.A.Center@uscg.mil. Offerors shall carbon copy John.R.Joeckel2@uscg.mil on quote submissions. Quotes must be received no later than 1700 EST on 9 September 2026. Each quotation shall include: 1. Total firm-fixed-price for all CLINs. 2. Manufacturer name and model number. 3. Product literature, specifications, or cut sheets sufficient to demonstrate compliance with all minimum technical requirements. 4. Warranty information. 5. Proposed delivery lead time in days ARO. 6. Confirmation that all items offered are new. 8. EVALUATION Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose quotation: 1. Is technically acceptable; 2. Meets the delivery requirement; and 3. Offers the lowest total evaluated price. Technical acceptability will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis against the minimum technical requirements in this solicitation. Failure to provide sufficient technical documentation may render a quotation technically unacceptable. 9.
